title: Israeli Man Critically Wounded in West Bank Shooting Amid Escalating Mideast Tensions【AP】
body:
An Israeli civilian was critically wounded in a shooting near the city of Qalqilya in the occupied West Bank on Friday, and a separate incident saw Israeli forces kill a Palestinian man who tried to ram a vehicle into soldiers in the same territory. Both attacks unfolded within hours of the start of the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur, intensifying already heightened tensions across the region and prompting renewed calls for restraint from both Israeli and Palestinian leaders.

The first incident occurred in the early afternoon when a gunman opened fire on a passing Israeli driver on a road linking the settlement of Ofra to the West Bank city of Qalqilya. The victim, identified by Israeli authorities as a 45‑year‑old man from the settlement of Kfar Etzion, suffered multiple gunshot wounds and was rushed to a hospital in Ramallah, where doctors say he remains in critical condition. Security forces quickly cordoned off the area, and a suspect—a 22‑year‑old Palestinian from Qalqilya—was apprehended after a brief chase. The man was taken into custody by the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) and is being held for questioning.

In a separate engagement about 30 kilometres east of Qalqilya, Israeli troops reported that a Palestinian man attempted to use a pickup truck to ram a line of soldiers conducting a routine patrol near the town of Nablus. The driver, who was later identified as a 28‑year‑old resident of the nearby village of Beita, allegedly accelerated toward the soldiers before being shot and killed by the soldiers’ gunfire. The IDF said the individual “intentionally tried to carry out a ramming attack” and that the response was necessary to protect the troops.

These two violent episodes come against a backdrop of escalating friction in the West Bank, where Israeli settlement expansion, frequent raids by the IDF, and a series of attacks on both civilians and soldiers have become increasingly common. Since the start of 2024, the number of Palestinian casualties in the occupied territories has risen sharply, according to data from the Palestinian Ministry of Health, while Israeli civilian deaths, though still relatively low, have also climbed. The timing of the attacks—just before Yom Kippur, the most solemn day on the Jewish calendar—has amplified their symbolic weight. Israeli officials have warned that any further violence during the holiday could trigger a “significant escalation,” while Palestinian leaders have condemned what they describe as “collective punishment” and called for an end to the occupation.

International reaction has been swift. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) issued a statement urging all parties to respect humanitarian law and to avoid actions that could endanger civilians. The United States, through its embassy in Jerusalem, expressed “deep concern” over the shooting and reiterated its support for Israel’s right to self‑defence, while also urging restraint to prevent a broader spiral of violence. The European Union’s foreign policy chief called for an immediate de‑escalation and highlighted the need for renewed dialogue between Israeli and Palestinian authorities.

Analysts note that the dual nature of the incidents—a targeted shooting of a civilian and an attempted vehicle‑ramming attack—reflects the evolving tactics of Palestinian militants, who have increasingly blended low‑tech assaults with more conventional armed attacks. Security experts warn that such diversification makes it harder for Israeli forces to predict and prevent future incidents, especially in densely populated areas where the line between combatants and civilians is blurred. At the same time, the rapid detention of the shooting suspect could be seen as an attempt by the IDF to demonstrate a swift response and deter further attacks during the holiday period.

As Yom Kippur unfolds, both sides are on high alert. Israeli security forces have bolstered their presence around major settlements and holy sites, while Palestinian activists have organized protests in several West Bank towns, calling for an end to what they label “systemic oppression.” The coming days will likely test the resilience of any cease‑fire mechanisms and could shape the trajectory of Israeli‑Palestinian relations for the remainder of the year. Observers hope that diplomatic channels, including back‑channel talks facilitated by regional actors, will gain traction before the violence escalates further, but the recent incidents underscore how fragile the situation remains.
